title: Genuine halt return
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and choose a mode for the loop host. For an input $x$, a configuration $c$ of $B$ on $x$, a natural number $t>0$, a Boolean word $w$, and a configuration $f$ of $F$ on $x$, suppose the run of $B$ from $c$ is live at every time $u<t$, does not enter state $a$ at any time $0<u<t$, and is halted at time $t$. Then the loop host run for $t$ steps from the non-startup call on $c$ with release set and no stop flag equals the non-startup call on the time-$t$ configuration of $B$, with release clear and stop flag true, retaining $w$ and $f$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean finite machines B and F
body run is live for every u < t
body run does not equal a at any 0 < u < t
body run is halted at time t
replaced:
Let $c$ be a body configuration and $t > 0$ a time such that the body stays live before
$t$, does not visit the anchor strictly between times zero and $t$, and is halted at
time $t$. Then the loop host, run for $t$ steps from the active released call on $c$,
reaches the stopped call on the body run at time $t$ with release clear and stop flag
$\mathrm{true}$, the complete body output captured, including any bit emitted by the
halting transition.
